title: Local-ring identifications with w-local target
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings identifying every local ring: for every prime $q\subset B$, the induced map $A_{q\cap A}\to B_q$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], then $B$ is ind-Zariski over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], that is, a filtered colimit of finite products of principal localizations $A_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

proof.text: Fix a finitely presented $A$-algebra $P$ and an $A$-map $u:P\to B$. Write $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_t)$ using [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For a maximal ideal $q$ of $B$, put $p=q\cap A$. Apply the inverse of the assumed $A_p\cong B_q$ to the elements $u(x_i)/1$. By the fraction description in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], write these inverse images as $a_i/s_i$ with $s_i\notin p$. Let $d=\prod_i s_i$ (empty product $1$); these fractions are elements of $A_d$.

Evaluate each $r_l$ on these fractions in $A_d$, and write its value as $N_l/d^{k_l}$. Its image in $A_p$ is zero, since the original map $u$ respects $r_l$. The fraction equality criterion in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives $t_l\notin p$ with $t_lN_l=0$ in $A$. Put $f=d\prod_l t_l$, so $f\notin p$. In $A_f$ every $s_i$ and $t_l$ is invertible (the inverse of a factor of $f$ is the complementary product times $f^{-1}$); hence every $r_l$ evaluates to zero. The polynomial substitution therefore descends to $v_q:P\to A_f$ and induces exactly the chosen map $P\to A_p$.

Write $v_q(x_i)=c_i/f^{h_i}$. The equality with $u$ in $B_q$ says that $\phi(f)^{h_i}u(x_i)-\phi(c_i)$ vanishes in $B_q$, where $\phi:A\to B$ is the given map. The same fraction equality criterion gives $b_i\notin q$ annihilating this numerator. Set $g_q=\phi(f)\prod_i b_i\notin q$. In $B_{g_q}$ all these numerators vanish and $\phi(f)$ is a unit. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] gives $A_f\to B_{g_q}$, and its composite with $v_q$ agrees with $u$ after localization, since it agrees on all the generators. Put $O_q=D(g_q)$, an open neighbourhood of $q$.

The $O_q\cap X^c$, for $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$, cover the closed-point set. By [lem-weil-pbc-w-local-partition], $X^c$ is profinite. Choose a clopen neighbourhood inside one of these opens for each closed point, then take a finite subcover by compactness. Successively subtract the preceding members to get a disjoint finite clopen partition subordinate to that subcover. The same cited lemma extends this partition uniquely to a clopen partition $X=\coprod_j U_j$, with each $U_j\subseteq O_{q_j}$. For $X=\varnothing$ this is the empty partition. This is precisely the topology needed here; no w-locality of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is assumed.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] to obtain idempotents $e_j$ with $U_j=D(e_j)$. For $i\ne j$, $e_ie_j$ is idempotent with empty basic open, so uniqueness in that lemma gives $e_ie_j=0$. Thus $e=\sum_j e_j$ is idempotent, and its basic open is all of $X$ (in any prime exactly one $e_j$ is outside it). Uniqueness gives $e=1$. The rings $B_j=e_jB$, with identity $e_j$, consequently satisfy $B\cong\prod_jB_j$: the forward map is $b\mapsto(e_jb)_j$ and the inverse is $(c_j)_j\mapsto\sum_jc_j$. Orthogonality checks both composites and multiplication. In the empty case the same uniqueness assertion gives $0=1$ in $B$.

A prime of $B_j=e_jB=B/(1-e_j)B$ contracts to a prime of $B$ in $D(e_j)=U_j$, and conversely contraction and quotient give inverse correspondences. Since $U_j\subseteq D(g_{q_j})$, the image of $g_{q_j}$ belongs to no prime of $B_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] it is a unit. Hence $B\to B_j$ extends to $B_{g_{q_j}}\to B_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property]. Composing the maps in step 3 and taking their product gives $P\to C=\prod_j A_{f_j}\to\prod_j B_j\cong B$ with composite $u$. We have proved the factorization for every finitely presented $P$, including the empty-product case.

Every algebra $C=\prod_{j=1}^m A_{f_j}$ is etale and finitely presented over $A$. Indeed the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] applied to $A\to A$ makes every $A_{f_j}$ etale. Now [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-product] makes $C$ etale, and clause (1) of the localization lemma makes $C$ finitely presented. The product lemma explicitly includes $m=0$.

Let $\mathcal E$ be the set of the fixed finite products $\prod_{j=1}^m A_{f_j}$ (including the empty product). By step 7 every member of $\mathcal E$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra. Step 6 says that every map from a finitely presented $A$-algebra to $B$ factors through some member of $\mathcal E$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-factorization-criterion-filtered-colimit] to this set and factorization property gives a small filtered category of members of $\mathcal E$ whose colimit is $B$.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: “Take all finite products of principal localizations equipped with an $A$-map to $B$”; factorization-criterion application made explicit

proof.text: By steps 7--8, $B$ is a filtered colimit of etale, finitely presented $A$-algebras, each a finite product of principal localizations $A_f$. This is the ind-Zariski presentation required by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].
